newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London stood mixed within tight ranges as the market shut for Christmas holidays and will not re-open until December 27. January closed $4.00 higher at $1,280 per tonne, while March gave up $3.00 to close at $1,235 per tonne. Sentiment was undermined by the new US certified coffee stock data which nearly tripled in the week ending December 20 to 34,315 bags. But the reaction was somewhat muted with most players away. In New York arabica futures closed higher across the board as dealers ignored supply figures showing a sharp build-up in exchange-certified stocks. US certified coffee stocks climbed by 21,744 bags in the week ended December 20, to 34,315 bags, as Latin American growers stepped up shipments to the United States. While the figures were expected to keep prices under pressure, traders said a round of position adjustments by speculators ahead of the holidays gave the market a small boost today. However, the stock figures may trigger a delayed sell-off after the New Year's Day Holiday. March rose by 1.65 cents/lb to close at 114.75 cents/lb while May added 1.70 cents/lb at 112.30 cents/lb. FUNDAMENTALS

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks nearly trippled in the week ended December 20, rising by 21,744 bags to 34,315 bags (12,571 bags). There were no bags pending grading in exchange-certified warehouses, the CSCE said. Most of this week's sharp build occurred in Miami, where stocks of Guatemalan coffee jumped to 17,250 bags, from 12,250 bags a week ago. Inventories of Venezuelan coffees reached 6,000 bags as of December 20.

JAPAN - Japan imported 440,183 bags of green coffee in November 1996, which compares to 324,938 bags the same month last year. That brought total imports of green coffee since the beginning of 1996 up to 5.049 million bags, significantly up on last year's figure of 4.738 million bags. The largest suppliers of green coffee in November 1996 were Indonesia (5,949 vs 4,376 bags), Colombia (4,462 vs 4,137 bags) and Brazil (8,618 vs 5,129 bags).

SWITZERLAND - Switzerland imported 79,998 bags of coffee in October 1996, 22 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 922,000 bags, 7.4 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5 per cent to 1.048 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Costa Rica (82,300 vs 84,700 bags), Brazil (89,600 vs 133,200 bags) and Colombia (109,700 vs 82,800 bags). The country exported 198,900 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 38 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 9.5 per cent to 184,500 bags.
